items.title: Bobby Militello interviewed by Monk Rowe, Buffalo, New York, October 14, 2002
items.q: Actually he first needed an alto player so he called Mike Migliore, who was with the band, with New Wave too.

ctx.x: Yeah. And we weren’t making any money at all. I think I made five grand that whole year. And I learned more and broke more plateaus in soloing and the understanding of jazz during that period I think, almost than during any period of my life. We were working at it and we were grooving. Absolutely grooving. And it was a great thing. During that period is when Maynard heard us opening up at the Landmark, which was a big bowling alley, but Maynard was playing in the banquet room here in Buffalo and we were opening…

bought the one with the B flat. Maynard said that was cool, I didn’t have to worry about it. All the writers hated me because they all wrote low A’s. But that didn’t bother me either. So I started playing bari with Maynard. And that was a childhood dream. That, and playing with Brubeck were both childhood dreams. And so that was really my first big break as far as now playing with someone big. Previous to that in Buffalo here I had gotten to play with/back up Ella Fitzgerald and Tony Bennett.
